system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty cap: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | Higher cap, ideally 50–100% for business warranties, with separate uncapped/price-capped fundamental, tax and specific indemnities. | **Reject 20% as sole remedy; increase and separate categories** — AUD 4.8m may be inadequate against material operational, IP, privacy or tax exposures. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket. | Lower de minimis and basket, or at least a tipping basket once exceeded; exclude known/specific indemnities, tax, title and fraud. | **Amend** — a deductible basket is acceptable in principle, but should not erode recovery for discrete known risks or protected claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months; Seller says limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | General warranties survive at least 18–24 months; longer periods for tax, IP, privacy/data, employment and fundamental matters. | **Amend expressly by category** — a blanket 18-month period can expire before latent tax, IP, privacy and employment liabilities emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limit. | Title, capacity, authority and ownership warranties uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with a substantially longer survival period. | **Reject** — Buyer needs full recourse if it does not receive the shares, clear title or valid authority it paid for. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations/exclusive remedies/non-reliance apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Express preservation of liability and remedies for fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate/reckless misrepresentation. | **Add express carve-out** — Seller must not use contractual limitations to shield dishonesty. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly, specifically and clearly disclosed against identified warranties, with sufficient detail to assess nature and consequences. | **Reject general disclosure** — data-room dumping improperly transfers diligence and interpretation risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers, including matters discoverable from data room/public records. | At most, exclude actual knowledge of specified Buyer deal-team members, not constructive knowledge or adviser knowledge; no bar for fraud or inadequate disclosure. | **Reject/replace** — “discoverable” knowledge and imputed adviser knowledge would gut the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; regards consent satisfied on delivery of written consent. Bluefen is c. AUD 3.6m / 30% FY26 revenue; conditions remain unproven. | Completion condition requiring valid, unconditional (or Buyer-approved) consent and satisfaction/waiver of all conditions, or a price holdback/termination right. | **Make a Buyer-benefit CP with evidence requirement** — loss or restriction of this customer would be material. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | c. AUD 3.2m facility to be released following Completion; not repaid and no final security discharge currently provided. | Repayment and irrevocable release/discharge of all Company and Seller-related security at or before Completion, funded from Seller proceeds; evidence as a completion deliverable. | **Reject post-Completion release** — debt-free/cash-free requires Buyer to receive the Company free of financial debt and security at Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420k conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. On-costs unknown. | Seller bears and funds all bonuses, payroll tax, superannuation and other costs; express indemnity and completion adjustment/escrow if not paid at Completion. | **Document and deduct/escrow the full exposure** — otherwise Buyer may inherit a Completion-triggered employment liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; c. AUD 180k remains open; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Specific indemnity covering all IP ownership/use/title defects and losses, plus delivery of cleared-payment evidence and irrevocable IP assignment/confirmation before Completion. | **Expand and condition Completion** — payment of one invoice does not itself establish that Buyer receives all necessary IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident; possible export of c. 1,240 records; no confirmed access, scope, notification requirement or quantified loss; Seller considers immaterial. | Ongoing investigation, prompt updates, remediation and regulatory/cooperation covenants; specific indemnity or escrow for all incident-related losses and a condition/termination right if material. | **Treat as a live identified risk** — privacy exposure may crystallise after Completion and cannot be dismissed as preliminary. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are characterised as ordinary-course costs; avoidability/accrual/termination unknown. | Full contracts and confirmation of term, termination rights, liabilities and approvals; prohibit renewals outside ordinary course and adjust/indemnify non-ordinary or undisclosed commitments. | **Require clarification and protection** — aggregate commitments may be a pre-Completion liability or value leakage, not routine expenditure. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks general limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance across all claims; tax/IP under general regime. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, known specific risks, covenants and fraud; no cross-application unless expressly agreed. | **Insist on separate regimes** — known and inherently long-tail risks need tailored caps, thresholds and survival periods. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; says it is merely the source relied on. | Completion deliverables: original/updated register, executed transfers, share certificates (if any), board approvals, ASIC records as applicable, releases of encumbrances and a title warranty. | **Require documentary completion verification** — a data-room register alone is not sufficient proof of clean, transferable title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity and tax deed mechanics; robust IP warranties and specific Ironquay protection, with longer survival and separate liability treatment. | **Reject** — tax and IP risks are potentially material, long-tail and unsuitable for the general cap/time-bar regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
